title: Common-stage additive and shift calculus
statement:
The equivalence relation of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category] is
reflexive, symmetric, and transitive. Transport is additive and obeys
$(u_N)_P=u_P$ for $M\subset N\subset P$. The common-stage operations are
representative-independent and make $\mathcal P_T$ an additive category.
Every finite diagram of objects, morphisms, composites, and asserted
equalities in $\mathcal P_T$ is represented over one finite field, and an
asserted equality holds exactly when it holds after passage to a further
common stage.

Define
$$
 (E,K)[1]=(E,K[1])
$$
and, for $f=[M,u]:(E,K)\to(F,L)$, define
$$
 f[1]=\left[M,
 \sigma_{M/F,L}^{-1}\circ u[1]\circ\sigma_{M/E,K}\right].
$$
This gives a well-defined additive autoequivalence $[1]$ with inverse
$[-1]$, and every finite-stage inclusion
$j_E:\mathcal C_E(T)\to\mathcal P_T$ commutes with shifts through the
specified comparison.

09P8](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09P8)). Difference: Stacks
computes the colimit of a diagram in one fixed category, whereas the colimit
here indexes a category, so addition, composition, shifts and finitely many
asserted equalities must first be transported to one common stage.

proof.text: We first supply the finite-stage additive and shift laws used below. In the ambient derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], binary direct sums are biproducts, and the shift is the reindexing complex with negated differential. Tensoring module sheaves distributes over a binary sum: the inverse maps are $(x,y)\otimes z\mapsto(x\otimes z,y\otimes z)$ and $(x\otimes z,y\otimes w)\mapsto(x,0)\otimes z+(0,y)\otimes w$, first on sections and then on sheafifications [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The total-tensor formula [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] gives the corresponding chain isomorphisms and commutation with shifts: the identification $P[1]\otimes Q\to(P\otimes Q)[1]$ is the identity on reindexed summands; for $P\otimes Q[1]\to(P\otimes Q)[1]$ multiply the summand of first-factor degree $p$ by $(-1)^p$. In the latter formula the first differential changes the multiplier from $(-1)^p$ to $(-1)^{p+1}$, and the second differential already has the negated differential of $Q$, giving precisely the negative total differential. Reversing these identifications gives the negative-shift formulas. By the definition of K-flatness, zero, finite sums and shifts of K-flat complexes remain K-flat: tensoring an acyclic complex gives respectively zero, a finite sum of acyclic complexes, or a shift of one [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Thus K-flat resolutions [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] compute reductions and the Koszul towers [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion] of sums and shifts by sums and shifts of those of their inputs. The coefficient-datum reduction functor [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] supplies the natural reduction normalizations; the foregoing chain isomorphisms commute with the transition maps $1\otimes q$.

source.place: ## Proof, finite-stage additive category laws, expanded at complex level

proof.text: For the finite-stage category laws used below, use the full stated hypothesis that $T_{F/E}:\mathcal C_E(T)\to\mathcal C_F(T)$ is an exact functor [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], not merely flatness of $F/E$. By [def-weil-triangulated-category], an exact functor is an additive functor between pre-triangulated categories, whose categories are additive and whose shifts are additive automorphisms. Apply this assertion with $F=E$, where $T_{E/E}=1$. It supplies the finite-stage zero object, binary biproducts, Hom abelian groups, bilinear composition and inverse shifts that this proof needs. Thus we use the stage structures included in the existing exactness package; we do not independently assert that inverse image of an infinite completed-module limit commutes with that limit on a refined stratum. The shift is the signed reindexing of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] on the full integral subcategory [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] and the same objects in [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. It is $\mathcal O_E$-linear by its chain formula. The Hom localization [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization] acts by $f\otimes a\mapsto f[1]\otimes a$, so identities, composition, addition and the inverse shift descend. The biproduct maps satisfy their five equations after tensoring with $1$. These explain the concrete finite-stage structures used in the common-stage calculations without proving, or assuming, any identification with Stacks' constant-coefficient category.

source.place: ## Proof, finite-stage additive category laws and finite-stage shift laws

proof.text:
For transport write $A_X=a_{N,M,E,K}$, $A_Y=a_{N,M,F,L}$, $B_X=a_{P,N,E,K}$, $B_Y=a_{P,N,F,L}$, $C_X=a_{P,M,E,K}$, $C_Y=a_{P,M,F,L}$. Put $H=T_{N/M}$, $G=T_{P/N}$, $J=T_{P/M}$, and $b=a_{P,N,M}:GH\xrightarrow{\sim}J$. The pentagon in [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] gives $B_XG(A_X)=C_Xb_{T_{M/E}K}$ and the analogous equation for $Y$. Naturality of $b$ gives $b_YGH(u)=J(u)b_X$. Substituting in the transport formula of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category] yields
$$ (u_N)_P=B_YG(A_Y)GH(u)G(A_X)^{-1}B_X^{-1}=C_YJ(u)C_X^{-1}=u_P. $$
The unit equations give $u_M=u$. Exact functors are additive by [def-weil-triangulated-category], so each $T_{N/M}$ is additive. Distributivity of composition with fixed associators now gives $(u+v)_N=u_N+v_N$, $0_N=0$, and $(-u)_N=-u_N$.

Reflexivity has witness $M$ since $u_M=u$, and symmetry follows by reversing the equality. If $(M,u)\sim(N,v)$ at $P_1$ and $(N,v)\sim(Q,w)$ at $P_2$, the finite compositum $P=P_1P_2$ exists by the directed-field data in [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]. Transporting both equalities and using step 3 gives $u_P=v_P=w_P$, which witnesses transitivity. No injectivity of the transport maps is assumed.

For two composable arrows at $M$, the transported composite satisfies
$$ v_Nu_N=a_ZT(v)a_Y^{-1}a_YT(u)a_X^{-1}=a_ZT(vu)a_X^{-1}=(vu)_N, $$
and transport of an identity is an identity. If inputs are replaced by equivalent representatives, take the compositum of their equality witnesses and the two proposed operation fields; by step 3 the corresponding inputs coincide there. The displayed identity and additivity then make the outputs of addition, negation and composition coincide there. Thus the operations in [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category] are independent of the field and representatives. All abelian-group, associativity, identity and bilinearity equations are verified by putting their finitely many representatives over one stage and applying the finite-stage laws established in step 2.

source.place: ## Proof, independence of common-stage operations and category laws

proof.text: There is also a zero object and every binary biproduct, as required by [def-weil-additive-category]. Take $Z=(\Ql,0)$. Scalar extension sends the zero identity to the zero identity, so every transport of $0$ is a zero object; every representative to or from $Z$ is therefore zero. For $X=(E,K)$ and $Y=(F,L)$ choose $M\supseteq E,F$ and take $B=(M,T_{M/E}K\oplus T_{M/F}L)$. Represent the four inclusions and projections at $M$ by the finite-stage ones. The equations $p_ii_j=\delta_{ij}$ and $i_1p_1+i_2p_2=1$ hold at $M$, hence on classes by step 5; the identity of $X$ is represented there by the identity of $T_{M/E}K$, and likewise for $Y$. These prove that $B$ is a biproduct. Together with the Hom abelian groups and bilinear composition of step 5, this makes $\mathcal P_T$ additive.

source.place: ## Proof, zero object and binary biproducts

proof.text: For $X=(E,K)$ and $N\supseteq E$ construct $\gamma_{N,X}:X\to(N,T_{N/E}K)$ by the representative $(N,1_{T_{N/E}K})$; the same identity represents a map in the opposite direction. By the unit equations their composites are the two identity classes, so these maps are inverse. For $f=[M,u]:X\to Y$ and $N\supseteq M$, all three maps in $\gamma_{N,Y}f\gamma_{N,X}^{-1}$ are represented at $N$; the outer maps are identities and the middle map is $u_N$. Thus this conjugate is $j_N(u_N)$. This constructs the object identifications mentioned but not defined in the blueprint proof.

source.place: ## Proof, finite-diagram sentence, explicit object identifications

proof.text: For a finite diagram take the compositum of the coefficient fields of its objects and the representative fields of its arrows, and use step 7 to replace every object by its isomorphic scalar extension at this field. By step 5 all specified composites are represented by the corresponding composites there. An asserted equality of parallel composites holds in $\mathcal P_T$ if and only if its two representatives become equal at a further field, by the equivalence relation in [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]. Take the compositum of the witnesses for the finitely many asserted equalities. Step 3 preserves each witness equality at this common field, giving all equations simultaneously. The reverse implication uses that field as a witness for each equality. An empty diagram may use $\Ql$. If just the list of equalities is empty, no witness extension is required: keep the field already containing the diagram's object and arrow fields. Representation of objects is through the displayed isomorphisms, not literal equality of pairs.

source.place: ## Proof, finite diagrams and simultaneous equality detection

proof.text:
Write $s_X=\sigma_{M/E,K}$, $s_Y=\sigma_{M/F,L}$, $h_X=\sigma_{N/M,T_{M/E}K}$, $h_Y=\sigma_{N/M,T_{M/F}L}$, and let $A_X=a_{N,M,E,K}$ and $A'_X=a_{N,M,E,K[1]}$, with analogous notation for $Y$. Associator compatibility of the natural shift comparisons [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] is
$$ \sigma_{N/E,K}A'_X=A_X[1]h_XT_{N/M}(s_X). $$
Naturality gives $h_YT_{N/M}(u[1])=(T_{N/M}u)[1]h_X$. Insert both identities and the transport formula into $S_N(u_N)$, where $S_M(u)=s_Y^{-1}u[1]s_X$; the adjacent inverse comparisons cancel, leaving
$$ S_N(u_N)=A'_YT_{N/M}(S_M(u))(A'_X)^{-1}. $$
Consequently equivalent representatives give equivalent shifted representatives. At a common stage, $S_M(v)S_M(u)=S_M(vu)$ by cancellation of the middle $s_Ys_Y^{-1}$, $S_M(1)=1$, and $S_M(u+v)=S_M(u)+S_M(v)$ by the additive finite-stage shift of step 2. Thus the formula in the statement defines a well-defined additive endofunctor.

source.place: ## Proof, shift well-definedness, explicit compatibility calculation

proof.text:
Compute with the signed chain-reindexing shifts, for which $K[-1][1]=K=K[1][-1]$ and the inverse identities on chain maps are literal [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; in a choice with inverse identifications, insert the corresponding natural unit and counit in these equations. Write $q_{M/E,K}=(\sigma_{M/E,K[-1]})[-1]:(T_{M/E}K)[-1]\to T_{M/E}(K[-1])$ and $\tau_{M/E,K}=q_{M/E,K}^{-1}$. Define $R_M(u)=\tau_{M/F,L}^{-1}u[-1]\tau_{M/E,K}$. For $H=T_{N/M}$ put $A_X=a_{N,M,E,K}$ and $A_X^-=a_{N,M,E,K[-1]}$, with analogous notation for $Y$. Apply $[-1]$ to the positive comparison equation of step 9 at $K[-1]$ and use naturality of the $H$ comparison at $\sigma_{M/E,K[-1]}$. It reads
$$q_{N/E,K}A_X[-1]=A_X^-H(q_{M/E,K})q_{N/M,T_{M/E}K}.$$
Multiplying by inverse $q$ factors gives
$$\tau_{N/E,K}A_X^-=A_X[-1]\tau_{N/M,T_{M/E}K}H(\tau_{M/E,K}).$$
Naturality gives $\tau_{N/M,T_{M/F}L}H(u[-1])=(Hu)[-1]\tau_{N/M,T_{M/E}K}$. Substitution cancels the two middle $\tau$ factors and yields
$$R_N(u_N)=A_Y^-H(R_M(u))(A_X^-)^{-1}.$$
This is the equality required for representative independence. At one stage the equations are explicitly $R_M(v)R_M(u)=\tau_Z^{-1}v[-1]\tau_Y\tau_Y^{-1}u[-1]\tau_X=R_M(vu)$, $R_M(1)=\tau_X^{-1}\tau_X=1$, and $R_M(u+v)=\tau_Y^{-1}(u[-1]+v[-1])\tau_X=R_M(u)+R_M(v)$; step 5 passes them to classes. For the inverse composites put $s_X=\sigma_{M/E,K}$ and $t_X=\sigma_{M/E,K[-1]}$, and use the corresponding $Y$ notation. Since $\tau_{M/E,K[1]}=(s_X[-1])^{-1}$ and $\tau_{M/E,K}[1]=t_X^{-1}$, the two calculations are
$$R_M(S_M(u))=s_Y[-1](s_Y[-1])^{-1}u\,s_X[-1](s_X[-1])^{-1}=u,$$
$$S_M(R_M(u))=t_Y^{-1}t_Y\,u\,t_X^{-1}t_X=u.$$
Represent the finite-stage inverse-shift unit and counit at $E$ for $(E,K)$. The displayed equations prove their naturality at the representative stage $M$ of every arrow, and their two triangle composites at a common stage are the identity chain-reindexing maps. This gives an inverse equivalence $[-1]$. Finally $j_E(K)=(E,K)$ and $j_E(u)=[E,u]$ preserve identities, composition and sums by step 5. With normalized identity associators, the shift compatibility equation at $E= M=N$ is $\sigma_{E/E,K}=\sigma_{E/E,K}^2$. Invertibility therefore gives $\sigma_{E/E,K}=1$. The formula at $M=E$ yields $j_E(u)[1]=[E,u[1]]$, and the objects agree as well, giving the specified inclusion-shift comparison.
